title: Note staleness lifecycle: create baseline → lazy refresh → verifyNote
answers: How does a note become stale?
How is a stale note re-verified?
What triggers refresh of note status?
Where are dependency hashes computed and compared?
body:
Note staleness lifecycle: create baseline → lazy refresh → verifyNote. No file watcher; staleness is detected lazily.

1. Create: src/ops.js:createNote → extractDeps (parses path:Symbol from body) → resolveDeps → src/deps.js:hashDep (findSymbol/blockEnd, sha/norm; falls back to file hash + symbolMissing). Saves verified, verifiedCommit=gitHead(repo), status 'fresh' via src/store.js:Store.put.

2. Code edit: nothing happens until something calls refresh.

3. Detect: src/ops.js:refresh → src/deps.js:checkNote (re-hash all deps; records reason when: file removed / symbol not found / symbol body changed / file changed). When a stored hash no longer matches, checkNote first checks if the code was unchanged since verifiedCommit by hashing it at that commit: unchangedSinceVerified. If unchanged, the mismatch is due to the hasher changing, not the code; sets upgraded=true. Otherwise marks the reason.

4. Upgrade: When upgraded=true (hasher changed, code didn't), refresh updates the note's deps to the new hashes and persists without marking it stale.

5. Refresh callers: src/ops.js:orient (MCP orient, UserPromptSubmit hook via cli.js), src/ops.js:lookup, cli.js list/check/verify, optional git post-commit hook.

6. Serve: src/rank.js:rank multiplies stale score by 0.6; renderNote adds '⚠ STALE' line. Invalid scores -1 (never served).

7. Re-verify: src/ops.js:verifyNote (via cli.js verify [ids]/verifyAll or check --verify): prompt from src/ops.js:gitDiffFor (diff from note.verifiedCommit) + deps.js:symbolText → src/llm.js:complete with VERIFY_SCHEMA, model store.config().verifyModel (default haiku). still_valid: re-hash, fresh, confidence +0.05; update: also replaces body, old body pushed to history; invalid: status invalid + invalidReason.
